original_statement:
In one sentence, what is the user-facing outcome you want? A Rust workspace that adopts Aspergillus gets every ASP rule checked mechanically on commit, the same way Python and TypeScript consumers do, including two whole-workspace checks: the same function body defined twice, and the same concept declared as a type in more than one crate.
Who is it for? Who uses this and in what situation? Maintainers of Rust repositories that adopt Aspergillus (first consumer: lobaria, a Cargo workspace of 33 crates), and the exophial workers committing into them.
How does a person USE the finished thing — what do they SEE and DO? Describe the observable behavior, i.e. how you would demo it. A consumer copies or depends on aspergillus/rust (as it does today for rust/configs/clippy.toml) and runs the Rust rules over its workspace; each finding prints as `path:line: ASPnnn` and a finding in a blocking rule fails the run. docs/design.md's Rust column names, for every rule of Levels 2 and 3 and every ASP4xx rule that applies to Rust, the enforcing check: a clippy lint, a declarative ast-grep YAML rule under rust/ast-grep-rules/ (the engine TypeScript already uses under typescript/ast-grep-rules/), or a whole-workspace check; a rule the Rust language already enforces names the language feature, and a rule that does not apply to Rust says why. No entry reads 'Manual', 'planned' or 'Module structure'. A duplicate-function check reports two Rust functions whose normalized bodies are identical, as `aspergillus check-duplicates` does for Python. A duplicate-type check reports a struct or enum declared in one crate whose concept a type in another crate of the same workspace already declares, with an allowlist for intended cases.
What does 'done' look like in plain language? State the acceptance you could check without reading any code. Run against lobaria integrated a027fb9, the duplicate-type check reports the three declarations of Nanos (statechart/src/units.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs, hold-time-curve/src/input.rs) and of Receipt (statechart/src/edge.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs, hold-time-curve/src/input.rs) as findings. The ASP202, ASP204, ASP205 and ASP206 Rust checks each report a finding on a committed Rust fixture that violates the rule and none on a committed fixture that satisfies it, for every rule that has a Rust check. docs/design.md's Rust column has no 'Manual', 'planned' or 'Module structure' entry. A Rust consumer runs the checks with cargo and the ast-grep crates (ast-grep-core, ast-grep-config, ast-grep-language), with no Python or Node runtime in its gate path.
What are the non-goals / constraints? What must this NOT do? Not a change to the Python or TypeScript rules. Not autofix: report-only, as the other languages are. Not a dylint compiler plugin as the required engine: ast-grep YAML plus the ast-grep crates is the engine lobaria already runs (lobaria chart/src/ast_grep_gate.rs, lob-979). The duplicate-type check does not flag two types that share only a name when their shapes differ (lobaria's per-module Refused, Carried, Hit and Finding types are distinct types with local meaning).
Any examples or references? (links, prior art, a similar thing you like) aspergillus docs/design.md sections 'Level 2', 'Level 3', 'Catalog rules ASP4xx', 'Whole-project CLI tools' (check-duplicates, asp-21d); typescript/ast-grep-rules/*.yml; lobaria chart/src/ast_grep_gate.rs and scripts/gates/core-types-rules/*.yml (ast-grep YAML rules run on ast-grep-core/config/language 0.40.0 from Rust); lobaria integrated a027fb9: 454 pub type declarations carry 384 distinct names, 45 names declared more than once.
What priority is this? (P0–P4) and why now? P1

Decomposed child: Aspergillus must report the same concept declared as a type in more than one crate of a Cargo workspace. The check reports a struct or an enum declared in one crate whose concept a type in another crate of the same workspace already declares. The check has an allowlist for intended cases. Acceptance a person can check without reading code: run against lobaria integrated a027fb9, the check reports as findings the three declarations of Nanos (statechart/src/units.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs, hold-time-curve/src/input.rs) and the three declarations of Receipt (statechart/src/edge.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs, hold-time-curve/src/input.rs). The check does not flag two types that share only a name when their shapes differ. lobaria's per-module Refused, Carried, Hit and Finding types are distinct types with local meaning, and the check does not flag them. Each finding prints as `path:line: ASPnnn`. The check reports only; it does not autofix. The check runs with cargo and the ast-grep crates (ast-grep-core, ast-grep-config, ast-grep-language). No Python runtime and no Node runtime is in the consumer gate path. Reference: lobaria integrated a027fb9 carries 454 pub type declarations with 384 distinct names, and 45 names appear more than once. This deliverable does not change the Python rules or the TypeScript rules.
restatement: Aspergillus must gain one new check for a Cargo workspace. The check reads every crate of the workspace. It finds a concept that more than one crate declares as a type. A concept is a struct declaration or an enum declaration. The check compares the shape of the two declarations, not the name alone. Two types that carry the same name but different shapes are separate concepts, and the check keeps silent about them. A team accepts a duplicate on purpose in some cases, so the check reads an allowlist and drops a pair the allowlist names. The check writes one line for each finding. The line has the form `path:line: ASPnnn`. The check writes a report only. The check changes no file of the workspace under test. The check is a Rust program. Cargo builds it. It parses Rust with the ast-grep crates ast-grep-core, ast-grep-config and ast-grep-language. A consumer runs the check with no Python runtime and no Node runtime present. The lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9 is the reference corpus. That workspace declares 454 public types, 384 distinct names, and 45 names more than once. Against that corpus the check must name the three declarations of Nanos and the three declarations of Receipt. Against that same corpus the check must stay silent about the per-module Refused, Carried, Hit and Finding types, because each of those carries a local meaning. This work adds the Rust check only. It leaves the Python rules and the TypeScript rules as they are.

restatement_clauses.text: The check reports a struct or an enum declared in one crate of a Cargo workspace whose concept a type in another crate of the same workspace already declares.
Run against lobaria integrated a027fb9, the check reports as findings the three declarations of Nanos: statechart/src/units.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs and hold-time-curve/src/input.rs.
Run against lobaria integrated a027fb9, the check reports as findings the three declarations of Receipt: statechart/src/edge.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs and hold-time-curve/src/input.rs.
The check does not flag two types that share only a name when their shapes differ. The check does not flag lobaria's per-module Refused, Carried, Hit and Finding types.
The check has an allowlist for intended cases. The check drops a pair the allowlist names, and keeps every other finding.
The check reports only. The check does not autofix, and it changes no file of the workspace under test.
The check runs with cargo and the ast-grep crates ast-grep-core, ast-grep-config and ast-grep-language.
No Python runtime and no Node runtime is in the consumer gate path.
This deliverable does not change the Python rules or the TypeScript rules.

goal: Add a report-only Rust check that names a concept declared as a type in more than one crate of the same Cargo workspace, with an allowlist, verified against lobaria at a027fb9.
acceptance_criteria: Two small test workspaces are prepared. In the first, two different crates each declare the same concept as a type. In the second, one single crate declares the same concept twice. The check names the pair in the first workspace. The check names no pair in the second workspace.

The check runs over the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9. The report names all three places that declare Nanos: statechart/src/units.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs and hold-time-curve/src/input.rs.

The check runs over the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9. The report names all three places that declare Receipt: statechart/src/edge.rs, pump-strategy/src/units.rs and hold-time-curve/src/input.rs.

The check runs over the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9. The report names the Nanos and Receipt duplicates. The report names none of the per-module Refused, Carried, Hit or Finding types, which share a name but have different shapes.

The check runs over the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9. Every printed finding line has a file path, then a colon, then a line number, then a colon, then a space, then a rule code made of the letters ASP and three digits.

The check runs twice over the same workspace. The second run adds one duplicate pair to the allowlist. The second report omits that pair. The second report keeps every other finding of the first report.
A throwaway copy of the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9 is made. The check runs over the copy and prints findings. No file of the copy is added, deleted or modified afterwards.
Cargo builds the check from a clean build directory and the build succeeds. The built program's dependency list contains all three crates ast-grep-core, ast-grep-config and ast-grep-language.
A consumer runs the check over the lobaria workspace at integrated a027fb9 on a machine where no python3 program and no node program can be found. The check still prints its findings.
The list of files this work changed is compared with the state of the repository before the work started. No file of the Python rules and no file of the TypeScript rules appears in that list.
